overview.problem: A ~2,900 LOC simavr-based emulation/test harness already exists under /Users/admin/offline/Nava-Firmware/sim/ (untracked, authored in one session, never built or executed). It is blocked from building by two concrete defects plus one unverified alignment concern: (1) simavr.version pins a fabricated commit hash (a16e8d31c4dc2b0d7a66c27f8f7f5e1a2b3c4d5e, sequential-hex fake) which hard-fails setup_simavr.sh under `set -e`; (2) the keg-only Homebrew libelf dependency that both simavr's sim_elf.c and the harness `-lelf` link require is absent and, even once installed, not on default search paths; (3) the harness core calls avr_make_mcu_by_name("atmega1284") with an inline comment asserting that is simavr's registry name for the ATmega1284P core, while the built ELF reports mmcu atmega1284p — these two identifiers (simavr's internal core-registry name vs the ELF's embedded mmcu string) are independent and need not match, so the correct argument must be determined empirically at build time, not assumed. The 13-case regression suite (Timer1 PPQN clock, 2ms Timer2 trigger-off, Timer3 flam, shuffle offsets, bar-end pattern swap, EXT_INST MIDI note on/off, SLAVE MIDI sync) has therefore never run and its green/red state is unknown.
overview.approach: Do NOT redesign — the scaffold is verified faithful to the firmware registers and matches the request spec point-for-point. Instead: unblock, build, execute, triage, and harden it. First repin simavr.version to a real build-verified commit (upstream HEAD 6a2c268c2e50a4ef0967f8a7bb281df9eed6c2bb, fall back to tag v1.7), plumb keg-only libelf paths into both setup_simavr.sh and sim/Makefile, and empirically confirm the avr_make_mcu_by_name argument against the linked simavr core registry (keeping the existing "atmega1284" + comment unless a probe proves it returns NULL). Rebuild libsimavr.a + hd44780.o via the vendored submodule, verify a clean `pio run -e nava_sysex` through the src symlink, then build the harness and drive `make -C sim test`. Because the suite has never executed, carry an explicit per-test triage loop that classifies every failure (harness-model bug / fixture bug / timing-window bug / genuine firmware finding) before touching code. Finally repair README drift. All system-mutating steps (brew install, submodule fetch, git commit) are consent-gated.
overview.goal: Green (or fully-triaged and explained) 13-case regression suite runnable via `make -C sim test`, a reproducible one-command build path, and documentation that matches the on-disk reality.

decisions.decision: Do NOT pre-commit to changing avr_make_mcu_by_name("atmega1284"). Treat the argument as an empirically-gated value: at build time probe the linked simavr core registry with both "atmega1284" and "atmega1284p", and keep whichever returns a non-NULL avr for this ELF. Change the string ONLY if the probe proves the current "atmega1284" fails.
decisions.reasoning: nava_sim.c line 158 carries an existing comment — `/* simavr names the ATmega1284P core "atmega1284" */` — asserting the current string is correct. simavr's internal core-registry name and the ELF's embedded mmcu string are independent identifiers that do not need to match each other. Assuming they must match (and blindly switching to "atmega1284p") could make avr_make_mcu_by_name return NULL, aborting nava_sim_create and breaking all 13 test binaries — the opposite of the goal. An empirical probe is the only safe way to resolve which name the linked simavr build actually registers.

constraints.text: simavr.version MUST hold a real commit that build-verifies libsimavr.a on macOS arm64 with Apple clang before setup_simavr.sh is declared working.
libelf include and lib paths MUST be added to both setup_simavr.sh and sim/Makefile; the keg-only default-path failure MUST be resolved.

The avr_make_mcu_by_name argument MUST be the string that returns a non-NULL avr for the linked simavr core; verify empirically at build time (probe both "atmega1284" and "atmega1284p"). Do NOT assume it must equal the ELF's mmcu string — simavr's core-registry name and the ELF mmcu are independent identifiers. Every one of the 13 regression cases MUST end in one of {PASS, triaged-and-explained}; no silently-skipped or unclassified failures.

Harness edits MUST NOT break the verified register anchors (CS pins, MSB-first byte orders, DAC channel/velocity encoding, muxAddr table, INH pins, DIN clk PA1, TRIG_OUT PA2, 31250 baud, +12 note offset, running status, 0xF8 UDR1 bypass).

The firmware ELF SHOULD be rebuilt via `pio run -e nava_sysex` (not reused blindly) because the working tree has dirty jjjjj_firmware/ edits that may diverge from the cached 64KB ELF.

invisible_knowledge.system: This is a native (arm64, Apple clang) simavr test harness that loads the AVR firmware ELF and drives it deterministically by cycle count. Tests boot the firmware for a fixed cycle budget, inject front-panel button presses and MIDI/EEPROM stimulus via simavr IRQs, run a bounded number of cycles, then assert against a cycle-stamped event log. The firmware uses an EXTERNAL I2C EEPROM (24LC1024 at bus addresses 0x50 lower / 0x54 upper), not the AVR's internal EEPROM — so the harness models a TWI device that must be seeded BEFORE the first boot-time LoadSeqSetup read. Observable outputs are captured via the 74HC595 LED/16-bit trigger word, the MCP4822 DAC velocity CV, PORTA[7:5] mux attribution, the HD44780 text mirror, and USART1 MIDI TX.
invariants: The avr_make_mcu_by_name argument must be the name the LINKED simavr build registers for the ATmega1284P core (determined empirically) — independent of the ELF mmcu string.
EEPROM must be seeded before nava_sim_run_cycles so the boot-time LoadSeqSetup read returns bpm=120/MASTER.
Timer math is derived with truncating integer division: OCR1A=(16000000/8)/FREQUENCY=10416; every period inherits that truncation.

Register-level device encodings are fixed: CS pins PB3/PB4/PD4/PD5, MSB-first shift order, DAC word 0x1000|(velocity>>5), muxAddr {0x00,0x80,0x40,0xC0,0x20}, 31250 baud, +12 MIDI note offset, running-status handling, 0xF8 realtime written straight to UDR1.
Peripheral models attach in dependency order: eeprom -> spi -> gpio -> lcd -> midi.
panel_latch[5] is the single source of truth for what the firmware reads through the 74HC165 chain.
tradeoffs: Cycle-exact assertions with small tolerance (CYCLE_TOLERANCE=32) buy precise regression detection at cost of fragility to ISR-entry latency.
Vendoring simavr as pinned submodule trades a one-time build for reproducibility and hd44780 example part sources.
In-process C EEPROM seeding trades a self-documenting .bin fixture for zero external-tooling dependency.
Pinning known firmware bugs as expected behavior trades correctness tests for regression-detecting tests.

Adding a `strings` probe satisfies the AC (`strings firmware.elf | grep 1284 confirms mmcu atmega1284p`) without adding a hard assertion — the mmcu string in the ELF is distinct from simavr's registry name, so we print it for the operator rather than failing on a specific value.

Implements DL-005 empirical gating: try "atmega1284" first (current documented name), fall back to "atmega1284p" if the former returns NULL. The structure guarantees the correct name is used regardless of which simavr build is linked, without pre-committing to an answer that may be wrong. --- a/sim/Makefile
+++ b/sim/Makefile
@@ -8,16 +8,22 @@ REPO_ROOT := $(realpath ..)
 SIMAVR    := $(CURDIR)/simavr
 BUILD     := $(CURDIR)/build
 ELF       := $(REPO_ROOT)/.pio/build/nava_sysex/firmware.elf
 
+# libelf is keg-only; resolve its prefix at make time so -I/-L are explicit.
+LIBELF_PREFIX := $(shell brew --prefix libelf 2>/dev/null)

 CFLAGS    := -arch arm64 -O2 -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -Wno-unused-parameter \
              -I$(SIMAVR)/sim \
              -I$(SIMAVR)/simavr/sim \
              -I$(CURDIR)/harness \
              -I$(CURDIR)/fixtures \
+             -I$(LIBELF_PREFIX)/include \
+             -I$(LIBELF_PREFIX)/include/libelf \
              -DNAVA_ELF_PATH=\"$(ELF)\"

              $(BUILD)/hd44780.o \

code_changes.comments: libelf is keg-only — `brew install libelf` places headers under /opt/homebrew/opt/libelf/include/{,libelf/} and the library under /opt/homebrew/opt/libelf/lib — none of which are on clang's default search paths. Using `brew --prefix libelf` at make time derives the correct prefix regardless of Homebrew's install location (Intel /usr/local vs Apple Silicon /opt/homebrew). The existing -lelf linker flag (line 25) requires the -L to resolve; the harness includes sim_elf.h which may pull in libelf headers transitively and requires the -I.

acceptance_criteria: `make -C sim test` runs all 4 binaries and reports each case's TAP line.
Every non-passing case carries a written classification and, where fixed, the minimal harness/fixture/test change with rationale.
The two pre-pinned firmware bugs remain pinned; no MUX_ATTR equality assertions are (re)introduced.
Any timing-window change is justified as ISR-entry jitter and stays integer-derived.
Final `make -C sim test` exit status is 0, or a documented residual set of quarantined cases with a simavr-limitation rationale.

code_intents.behavior: Add a `boot_wait_ready(ctx, max_cycles)` helper that uses nava_sim_run_until with an LCD-content predicate to detect firmware boot completion before asserting any events. Emit a diagnostic if the LCD stays blank for the full budget. Add a TAP diagnostic showing the ELF path at run start. The EEPROM-before-cycles invariant is already correctly implemented; confirm and comment it.

Add a NAVA_TWI_DEBUG conditional trace macro to twi_irq_cb for boot-config diagnosis (START and READ paths). Add a comment to the I2C_GOT_CHIP enum entry documenting why it is a dead state — the START handler resolves R/W and transitions directly to I2C_READING or I2C_ADDR_HI, intentionally bypassing I2C_GOT_CHIP. This diff is written against the POST-CI-011 state of nava_sim.c.

Replace `nava_sim_run_cycles(ctx, BOOT_CYCLES)` with `boot_wait_ready(ctx, BOOT_CYCLES)` in each timing test function. When no TRIG_WORD events appear after PLAY, emit the current LCD line 0 content as a diagnostic before calling test_fail, so the operator can distinguish a boot failure from a sequencer failure.
Replace `nava_sim_run_cycles(ctx, BOOT_CYCLES)` with `boot_wait_ready(ctx, BOOT_CYCLES)` in all four EXT_INST test functions. Preserve the accent-velocity=16 pin as an asserted expected value.

Replace `nava_sim_run_cycles(ctx, 8000000ULL)` with `boot_wait_ready(ctx, 8000000ULL)` in both SLAVE test functions. Add an LCD diagnostic before test_fail when no TRIG_WORD events appear after injected clock.

Fix the critical slot-1 fixture bug: fx_make_eeprom_image fills slots 1..127 with FX_PTRN_BASIC (all-BD), but the swap test needs slot 1 to be FX_PTRN_GROUP_B (all-SD) so trig_word bits distinguish the two patterns. Override the EEPROM image inside each test function (before boot_wait_ready) by calling fx_make_eeprom_image then fx_pattern_to_eeprom(&FX_PTRN_GROUP_B, img + FX_PTRN_SIZE) for slot 1. Update main() to use the TEST macro since EEPROM is now managed inside each fn. Replace BOOT_CYCLES with boot_wait_ready.

code_changes.comments: Declares the LCD-predicate boot helper used by all four test suites. Placed in test_runner.h so every test binary that includes test_runner.h gets it without additional headers. The function signature mirrors nava_sim_run_until's return convention (cycles consumed).

boot_wait_ready uses nava_sim_run_until with an LCD predicate rather than a fixed cycle count. This is the R-003 mitigation: if the firmware boots in 3M cycles it wastes no time; if it doesn't boot in BOOT_CYCLES the diagnostic explains why events are missing. The predicate checks lcd[0][0] != ' ' to skip the cleared LCD state (all spaces) that precedes the first firmware write. frontpanel.h added for fp_lcd_line consistency; nava_lcd_get_line is used directly since lcd.h is already included.

Written against the POST-CI-011 state of nava_sim.c (CI-011 touches only nava_sim_create at line ~155; this diff touches lines 29-124). TWI_DBG is zero-cost in production builds and activates with -DNAVA_TWI_DEBUG for R-004 diagnosis (boot config reads wrong). The I2C_GOT_CHIP comment documents why the state is never assigned — the START handler collapses the two transitions (chip-addressed + R/W determined) into a single step — which is the correct behavior, not a bug. No behavior changes; only diagnostics and documentation.

Replaces all blind BOOT_CYCLES sleeps with boot_wait_ready. This is the R-003 mitigation: if the firmware reaches its run loop in 3M cycles, the remaining 5M cycles are not wasted, and if it never boots the diagnostic explains the missing TRIG_WORD events. The LCD content check (fp_lcd_line is already available from frontpanel.h) distinguishes a boot failure from a sequencer failure, which are otherwise indistinguishable from a missing-events log. Timer math constants (NAVA_PPQN_PERIOD_CYCLES, NAVA_TRIG_OFF_CYCLES, NAVA_FLAM_CYCLES) are unchanged per C-005.

Mechanical substitution of blind boot wait with boot_wait_ready across all four EXT_INST test functions. No logic changes to note-on/off assertions, the +12 wire-note offset (FX_EXT_WIRE_BASE=48), or the FX_MIDI_ACCENT_VEL=16 pin — those remain exactly as designed per DL-009 and C-008.

The SLAVE tests re-seed the EEPROM inside the fn BEFORE any cycle steps, so boot_wait_ready correctly boots against the SLAVE config. The expanded diagnostic on n_trigs==0 distinguishes three failure modes: boot failure (LCD blank), USART1 RX injection not working, or wrong sync config in EEPROM — all of which would produce the same empty TRIG_WORD log without this text.

Fixes the critical fixture bug: fx_make_eeprom_image fills slots 1..127 with FX_PTRN_BASIC (all-BD), making slot 1 indistinguishable from slot 0 (also BD) by trig_word bits. The test cannot detect a swap that produces no change in the trigger word. The fix writes FX_PTRN_GROUP_B (all-SD) to slot 1 explicitly via fx_pattern_to_eeprom before boot, matching the pattern-swap test's stated design (TRIG_BD vs TRIG_SD as the discriminant). The EEPROM override uses the same pre-boot seeding pattern as test_midi_sync (override inside fn before any cycle steps), so the firmware's LoadSeqSetup read sees the correct config. main() switches from TEST_WITH_PATTERN to TEST since ptrn_change_sync is now encoded in the EEPROM image built by the fn, not passed through the test_entry_t.

diagrams.title: PPQN step-trigger flow under test (test_timing)
diagrams.mermaid:
sequenceDiagram
  participant T as test_timing
  participant S as nava_sim
  participant FW as firmware (Clock.ino)
  participant SPI as spi_bus (74HC595)
  participant L as event_log
  T->>S: run_cycles(BOOT_CYCLES)
  T->>S: fp_press/release PLAY
  T->>S: run_cycles(ONE_BAR_CYCLES)
  loop each PPQN tick (Timer1 CTC)
    FW->>FW: CountPPQN() every 83336 cyc
    FW->>SPI: write 16-bit trig word (step)
    SPI->>L: EVT_TRIG_WORD @cycle
    FW->>FW: Timer2 arm -> clear trig +32000 cyc
  end
  T->>L: find_first / find_nth EVT_TRIG_WORD
  T->>T: assert delta == 2000064 (+/- tol)

diagrams.title: I2C EEPROM model state machine (nava_sim.c twi_irq_cb)

stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> I2C_IDLE
  I2C_IDLE --> I2C_READING: START + addr 0x50/0x54, R=1
  I2C_IDLE --> I2C_ADDR_HI: START + addr 0x50/0x54, W=0
  I2C_IDLE --> I2C_IDLE: START + other addr
  I2C_ADDR_HI --> I2C_ADDR_LO: WRITE addr high
  I2C_ADDR_LO --> I2C_WRITING: WRITE addr low (+65536 if upper)
  I2C_WRITING --> I2C_WRITING: WRITE data byte (cur_addr++)
  I2C_READING --> I2C_READING: READ -> inject data byte (cur_addr++)
  I2C_WRITING --> I2C_IDLE: STOP
  I2C_READING --> I2C_IDLE: STOP
  I2C_ADDR_HI --> I2C_IDLE: STOP
  I2C_ADDR_LO --> I2C_IDLE: STOP
